newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine YPF wants to float staff shares.
newsitem.headline: Argentine YPF wants to float staff shares.

text.p: Argentine oil giant YPF SA said Wednesday it would shortly start formalities to float the 10 percent of its share capital currently in the hands of employees.

In a letter to the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, YPF said the offer of 35.3 million class C shares required the approval of 90 percent of staff and government approval of the early payment of debts run up by employees to buy the shares.
The privatized Argentine oil company said that "in coming days" it would present the relevant documents to Buenos Aires and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commissions.
"If the offer is carried out, the Argentine government will receive most of the funds from this share placement and the rest will be distributed among employees," said YPF.
"YPF will not receive any of the funds raised by this offer," the letter read.
YPF shares, a market bellwether, have recently broken resistance levels around $29 to set all-time highs.
Shares quoted in Buenos Aires closed before the announcement Wednesday at an all-time high of $29.9 and the ADRs closed at $30, near a recent all-time high of $30.25.
YPF was one of the first state companies to be privatized after the Peronist government of President Carlos Menem came to power in 1989.
